ai_complex_conflict.direction: Genuinely mixed and deliberately not averaged. An AI-capex break compresses SDGR's residual sentiment multiple while simultaneously destroying the 'AI replaces physics' narrative that has been compressing its competitive premium. Owning SDGR here approximates being short the AI-drug-discovery narrative and long the physics moat.

edge_explainer: The bear thesis the market priced - physics-based simulation losing to AI/ML co-folding - is REFUTED on four independent primary channels, and the refutation is the finding. Lilly acquired Ajax Therapeutics for up to $2.3B and wrote Schrodinger a ~$57M cheque on 2026-06-29 for a 5.8% stake in a molecule Schrodinger designed (8-K item 7.01); Top-20 Pharma ACV, the cohort most capable of building its own AI, grew the FASTEST at +15.3% in FY25; gross dollar retention held at 96%, so nobody is leaving; and Schrodinger co-published with BMS and Lilly in March and April 2026. Generative co-folding proposes structures, free-energy perturbation decides which are worth making - complements, priced as substitutes during the Jan-Mar 2026 narrative de-rate. This is an anti-masking result: the absence of expected erosion is itself the positive microstructure finding. The REAL bear, which nobody is discussing, is CONFIRMED and is worse than the narrative one: FY25 ACV grew only 4.0%, net dollar retention collapsed from 113% to 100%, and the >$1M commercial customer count fell from 29 to 27. The land-and-expand engine stalled. Gross retention at 96% with NDR at 100% localises it precisely as a usage/budget problem, not competitive displacement - consistent with the biopharma funding winter, inconsistent with AI substitution. Presentation check: on 2026-02-25 the company disclosed the 4% ACV and the NDR collapse, announced an accelerated hosted-software transition that mechanically depresses reported software revenue (which then fell 21% in Q1'26), and guided FY26 ACV to +10-15%, all in one release. That is disclosed bad news presented honestly - CLEAN under house doctrine, not a catch - but it means the company-defined, unaudited ACV metric is now doing all the work and must be tested rather than accepted. Testing it produces the operative finding: FY26 needs +$19.5M to +$29.5M of ACV; Q1 delivered +$3.0M and the Q2 guide implies +$0.7M to +$4.7M, so H2 must carry +$12M to +$26M. Trailing-four-quarter ACV is growing +2.8%, not the +12% single-quarter headline. On the EV question: EV is $714M pro-forma for the Ajax cash, or $821M including the $106.9M operating-lease liability, which is 3.55x to 4.08x TTM ACV of $201M. So software roughly EXACTLY covers the EV at a fair-to-full multiple - you are not getting the software free, and 3.5-4.1x revenue for a 74%-GM franchise at 100% NDR is fair rather than cheap. The correct statement is that you pay a fair price for the software and receive at zero incremental cost the drug-discovery business ($55-65M/yr, 16 royalty-bearing programs, up from 13), two clinical assets being shopped rather than self-funded, and an equity-stakes book that has just demonstrated it converts to cash. The margin of safety is the free options plus $5.73/share of net cash, not a discounted core. What makes it ownable rather than merely interesting is the cap structure: zero debt, zero preferred, no warrants, and a cumulative 2026-2028 burn of roughly $180-230M against $428M of pro-forma net cash, so the funding question is closed with $200-250M to spare and no raise required. The edge is arithmetic: at $15.28 the market implies a 49% bear probability against our 30%, and a debt-free company with 37.5% of its market cap in cash and a demonstrated stake-monetisation channel does not carry a 49% chance of the bear case. Mechanism for the knowledge graph: masking channel = a revenue-recognition transition announced in the same release as a demand deceleration, which lets a real accounting artifact absorb attribution that partly belongs to demand; signal channel = trailing-four-quarter ACV and the NDR/customer-count KPI table, which are immune to the recognition change; signal-to-price latency = one to two quarters, since ACV is disclosed quarterly but NDR only annually, which is why the Feb-2027 print is the thesis line rather than any of the interim ones.
top_unverifiable: The 2026-02-11 -12.1% capitulation day on 6x volume has NO identified cause. No 8-K was filed, the Q4'25 print was two weeks later, and the news channel returned nothing dated to that day; the best available context is a sector-wide AI-drug-discovery de-rate through Jan-Feb 2026. An unexplained 6x-volume 12% down day is a real hole - if it was a large holder liquidating or an index event it is noise, but if it was a customer or partner loss surfacing through a channel not read, the net-dollar-retention finding is worse than scored. The Aug-5 call Q&A should be read for it before tranche 1 is placed.
